correctness.rationale: Equation (1) follows from exact cut cancellation of the mean-zero graph Poisson equation. The pairwise path Lipschitz bound is attained simultaneously by the signed cut-distance ramp, so the norm formula is exact. Saturation of every positive cross-cut pair determines all norming functions. Root-depth sums give the sharp path upper bound with uniqueness; leaf edges give the sharp star lower bound with uniqueness. Explicit tree rerooting gives an O(n) algorithm. The pure-stdlib exact-rational checker independently compares Laplacian pseudoinverse matrices and cut distances on 1441 exhaustively enumerated labelled trees and 120 additional cases; finite checks support, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: A sharp induced operator norm for real graph Poisson inversion on every finite tree is a natural endpoint regularity/conditioning invariant. Its value varies from (2n-3)/n for stars to floor(n²/4)/2 for paths, an order-n² qualitative spread. The complete ramp equality classification and O(n) exact algorithm make the result useful for stability analysis of graph-based potential reconstruction, beyond a small finite calculation.
